title: Planning and Dependency Reasoning
purpose: Seed plan construction and dependency reasoning so Lantern can organize subproblems/actions into editable partial-order plans, identify prerequisites, parallel work, critical paths, resource conflicts and contingencies, and replan when evidence or goals change without treating plans as obligations.

concepts.definition: An editable model of actions/subproblems, dependencies, resources and conditions intended to move from a current state toward an authorized goal.
A bounded action/subproblem with prerequisites, expected outputs, resource needs, status and success/failure conditions.
A condition or output that must be satisfied before a dependent step can validly proceed.
Directed graph representing prerequisite/dependency relationships among plan steps.
Plan specifying only ordering constraints that are actually required, allowing unrelated steps to proceed in any order or parallel.
Steps can proceed concurrently when dependencies, shared resources and safety/authority constraints permit.
Dependency chain whose duration/latency determines earliest completion under the current plan model.
A step unable to proceed because a prerequisite, resource, authority or required information is unavailable.
Meaningful intermediate state/checkpoint used to assess progress, validation or decision points.
Limit on compute, memory, time, tools, people, budget, energy or other resources relevant to scheduling.
Two or more steps require an incompatible use of a limited resource at the same time.
Preplanned response to a specified uncertainty/failure/condition.
Evidence/state determining which plan branch should be followed.
Revision of the plan when assumptions, dependencies, resources, evidence, goals or constraints change.
State such as ready, active, blocked, waiting, complete, failed, skipped, cancelled or superseded.
Scheduling flexibility a step can have without delaying a relevant milestone/critical path under the current model.
Transfer of a step/output/context to another agent/person/system with explicit expectations and provenance.
Defined route for restoring a prior safe/working state if a change fails.
Persisted/validated state from which work can safely resume after interruption/failure.

guards.reason: Plans are means/models and may be replaced while preserving the goal.
Plans remain revisable when evidence, constraints or goals change.
Presentation order does not establish a logical prerequisite.
Shared resources, side effects, authority or interference can still block concurrency.
Critical path is a scheduling property, not value/importance.
Blocked means waiting on a dependency/resource/authority, not necessarily failure.
Other independent work may proceed while one branch waits.
Milestones are intermediate checkpoints unless defined as final success.
Past cost is not a reason to continue when expected future value is poor.
Time pressure can change scope/priorities but does not erase hard constraints.
Adaptive replanning is expected under uncertainty.
Checkpoint supports continuity/recovery but is not final success.

invariants: Plans are editable models serving goals; they are not goals or obligations.
Only genuine prerequisites create ordering constraints.
Partial-order planning is preferred over unnecessary serialization.
Parallel execution requires dependency, resource, side-effect and authority compatibility.
Blocked, waiting, failed, skipped, cancelled and complete are distinct states.
Critical-path status describes schedule sensitivity, not semantic importance.
External waits should not prevent unrelated useful work when resources/authority permit.
Material changes in evidence, resources, constraints or goals trigger replanning.
Sunk cost never justifies continuing a low-value plan.
Handoffs preserve context, requirements, expected output and acceptance criteria.
Risky changes preserve rollback/checkpoint paths when feasible.
Plans cannot grant authority to execute actions.

provenance.authoring_basis: Partial-order planning, dependency/scheduling theory, project/systems engineering and adaptive executive-control principles adapted to Lantern's Gate-3 and distributed hive architecture.
